ctx.x: No trombone? Yeah, Jim Robinson. Oh Jim, yeah. Well we stayed there for about two years I'd say. Yeah. Then Reverend Kershaw in the meantime when we was playing out there they came down here and heard different bands and they selected our band.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: I said, as long as you got me in drag, your band will never be broke up. No. But I said, as far as getting another man, I said, I'm more than sure you can get somebody to replace Jim and Howard.

ctx.x: Sure, they'd like to have the whole band.

Yeah, you see, but just like the band, I'm sure. Just like he said that they working this deal like they did before, bringing him over first and then bringing the band over afterwards, you know. So he was on the impression that his band was going to be broke up. I said, no, I said, as long as you got me in drag, your band will never be broke up. No. But I said, as far as getting another man, I said, I'm more than sure you can get somebody to replace Jim and Howard.
Yes, Jim doesn't want to travel much anymore.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: Because Jim used to get on me, Howard would get on me.

ctx.x: Did he say he wanted that?

Yeah. He wanted to start off on a cymbal and finish up on a cymbal like a swing band. See, I used to get angry, but I said, well, what can I do? He's the leader. He knows what he wants. But the balance of the fellas in the band would get angry with me. I said, it's not my fault. I said, y'all speak to the leader about it. I'm not playing the way I want to play. If I'm playing the way I want to play, I'll be playing the old style way. The way I'm supposed to play if I'm going to play authentic jazz. But I said, he…
Let me ask you about some of the earlier episodes again. Do you remember playing at Manny's? Manny's Tavern.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: George again on banjo, Elton Paneil on piano, drag on bass, Joe on drum.

ctx.x: Really? What was Howard playing? Yes. Trumpet.

Trumpet and trombone and that's all? That's all. We played, we played in 55, Broadway, when Joyce took sick. We didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no trumpet. We did not have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no clinic. And Joyce took sick. And Lewis Alcombe come, that, that night even his wife was our guest. Mm-hmm. And Joyce played two numbers, they, two, three numbers, they took sick. And me and Howard played the whole dance with…

Oh yeah, we had a piano. He was playing that night. Yeah, he played piano. But I mean you played parties with just trumpet and trumpet on no rhythm? No, no rhythm. No rhythm. Well, how did you keep the beat going? Beat with your feet.
